text: Which organelle is known as the powerhouse of the cell?
explanation: The mitochondria produces ATP through cellular respiration, supplying energy to the cell. It is therefore called the powerhouse of the cell.

text: The cell theory states that all living things are made up of
explanation: The cell theory, proposed by Schleiden and Schwann, states that all living organisms are composed of one or more cells, and the cell is the basic unit of life.

text: Which part of the cell controls all its activities?
explanation: The nucleus contains the genetic material (DNA) which directs all cellular activities including growth, metabolism, and reproduction.

text: The movement of water molecules from a region of higher water potential to a region of lower water potential through a semi-permeable membrane is called
explanation: Osmosis is specifically the movement of water through a selectively permeable membrane from a dilute solution (high water potential) to a concentrated solution (low water potential).

text: Which organelle is responsible for protein synthesis?
explanation: Ribosomes are small organelles found in the cytoplasm or on the rough endoplasmic reticulum. They translate mRNA into proteins.

text: The process by which substances move from a region of high concentration to a region of low concentration is called
explanation: Diffusion is the passive movement of particles from an area of high concentration to low concentration along a concentration gradient. No energy is required.

text: A cell placed in a hypertonic solution will
explanation: In a hypertonic solution, the external concentration is higher than inside the cell, so water leaves the cell by osmosis, causing it to shrink or undergo crenation (in animal cells) or plasmolysis (in plant cells).

text: The rigid outer covering of a plant cell is called the
explanation: The cell wall is made of cellulose and provides structural support and rigidity to plant cells. Animal cells do not have a cell wall.

text: Which of the following is NOT found in a plant cell?
explanation: Centrioles are found in animal cells and lower plant cells. They are involved in cell division (forming the spindle). Mature plant cells do not contain centrioles.

text: The endoplasmic reticulum is described as 'rough' when it has
explanation: Rough endoplasmic reticulum (RER) has ribosomes attached to its surface, giving it a rough appearance. These ribosomes synthesise proteins that are then processed by the RER.

text: Turgidity in plant cells is caused by
optionA: loss of water from the vacuole
optionB: gain of water by osmosis into the vacuole
explanation: When a plant cell absorbs water by osmosis, the vacuole enlarges and pushes against the cell wall, making the cell firm and turgid. This maintains the plant's structural rigidity.

text: The Golgi apparatus is primarily responsible for
explanation: The Golgi apparatus (Golgi body) processes, packages, and distributes proteins and lipids received from the endoplasmic reticulum. It acts as the cell's postal system.

text: Which scientist first observed and described cells using a microscope?
explanation: Robert Hooke first observed cells in 1665 when he examined a thin slice of cork under his microscope. He named what he saw 'cells' because they reminded him of monks' rooms.

text: The semi-permeable membrane of a cell is the
explanation: The cell membrane (plasma membrane) is selectively permeable, controlling what enters and exits the cell. It is made of a phospholipid bilayer with embedded proteins.

text: Plasmolysis occurs in a plant cell when it is placed in
explanation: Plasmolysis is the shrinkage of the cytoplasm away from the cell wall when a plant cell loses water by osmosis in a hypertonic (concentrated) solution.

text: Which kingdom do mushrooms belong to?
explanation: Mushrooms are members of the kingdom Fungi. Fungi are eukaryotic organisms that are heterotrophic, absorbing nutrients from their environment. They differ from plants in lacking chlorophyll.

text: The binomial nomenclature system of naming organisms was introduced by
explanation: Carl Linnaeus (1707–1778) developed the binomial nomenclature system, where each organism is given a two-part Latin name: genus and species. For example, Homo sapiens.

text: Which of the following is the correct hierarchical order of classification from largest to smallest?
optionB: Kingdom, Phylum, Class, Order, Family, Genus, Species
explanation: The correct taxonomic hierarchy from broadest to most specific is: Kingdom, Phylum (Division for plants), Class, Order, Family, Genus, Species.

text: Organisms that make their own food are called
explanation: Autotrophs (producers) manufacture their own food using sunlight (photosynthesis) or chemical energy (chemosynthesis). Green plants are the most common autotrophs.

text: Which nutrient provides the most energy per gram?
explanation: Fats (lipids) provide approximately 9 kcal per gram, more than double the energy from carbohydrates or proteins (approximately 4 kcal per gram each). They are the most energy-dense macronutrient.

text: The deficiency of Vitamin C causes
explanation: Scurvy is caused by Vitamin C (ascorbic acid) deficiency. Symptoms include swollen, bleeding gums, fatigue, and poor wound healing. Vitamin C is essential for collagen synthesis.

text: Photosynthesis takes place in which organelle?
explanation: Chloroplasts contain chlorophyll, the green pigment that absorbs light energy. Photosynthesis (light and dark reactions) occurs within the chloroplast.

text: The overall equation for photosynthesis is
explanation: The equation 6CO₂ + 6H₂O + light energy → C₆H₁₂O₆ + 6O₂ summarises photosynthesis. Carbon dioxide and water are converted into glucose and oxygen using light energy.

text: The green pigment in plants responsible for absorbing light energy is
explanation: Chlorophyll is the primary photosynthetic pigment found in the thylakoid membranes of chloroplasts. It absorbs red and blue light most effectively and reflects green light, making plants appear green.

text: Which of the following factors does NOT directly affect the rate of photosynthesis?
explanation: The main limiting factors of photosynthesis are light intensity, CO₂ concentration, water, and temperature. Oxygen concentration does not directly limit the rate of photosynthesis.

text: The light stage of photosynthesis produces which of the following?
explanation: The light-dependent stage occurs in the thylakoid membranes. It uses light energy to split water (photolysis), producing ATP, NADPH (reduced NADP), and oxygen as a by-product.

text: Which type of respiration does not require oxygen?
explanation: Anaerobic respiration occurs in the absence of oxygen. In animals/yeast, glucose is partially broken down, producing lactic acid or ethanol and carbon dioxide with a small amount of ATP.

text: The complete oxidation of glucose in aerobic respiration produces
explanation: Aerobic respiration: C₆H₁₂O₆ + 6O₂ → 6CO₂ + 6H₂O + 38 ATP. Glucose is fully oxidised to carbon dioxide and water, releasing a large amount of energy (ATP).

text: Anaerobic respiration in yeast produces
explanation: In yeast (fermentation), glucose is converted to ethanol (alcohol) and carbon dioxide. This process is used in brewing and bread-making. Only 2 ATP molecules are produced.

text: The site of aerobic respiration in a cell is the
explanation: Aerobic respiration occurs in the mitochondria. The Krebs cycle occurs in the mitochondrial matrix, while oxidative phosphorylation occurs on the inner mitochondrial membrane.

text: The net yield of ATP from the complete aerobic respiration of one molecule of glucose is
explanation: Complete aerobic respiration of one glucose molecule yields approximately 36–38 ATP molecules. Glycolysis yields 2 ATP, Krebs cycle yields 2 ATP, and the electron transport chain yields about 34 ATP.

text: Which vessel carries blood from the heart to the lungs?
explanation: The pulmonary artery carries deoxygenated blood from the right ventricle of the heart to the lungs for oxygenation. It is the only artery that carries deoxygenated blood.

text: Which blood component is responsible for clotting?
explanation: Platelets (thrombocytes) are small cell fragments that aggregate at a wound site and initiate the clotting cascade, preventing excessive blood loss.

text: The xylem vessels in plants transport
explanation: Xylem vessels transport water and dissolved mineral salts from the roots upward to the leaves and other parts of the plant. Movement is upward (from root to shoot).

text: Which of the following drives the transpiration stream in plants?
explanation: The cohesion-tension theory explains water movement in xylem. As water evaporates from leaves (transpiration), tension is created that pulls water upward. Cohesion between water molecules maintains a continuous column.

text: Phloem vessels transport
explanation: Phloem conducts organic solutes (mainly sucrose and amino acids) manufactured in leaves to all parts of the plant — a process called translocation. Movement is in both directions.

text: The bicuspid (mitral) valve is found between the
explanation: The bicuspid (mitral) valve has two cusps and separates the left atrium from the left ventricle. It prevents backflow of blood into the left atrium when the left ventricle contracts.

text: The main nitrogenous excretory product in humans is
explanation: Humans excrete nitrogen mainly as urea, which is produced in the liver by the ornithine cycle (urea cycle) from the breakdown of excess amino acids. Urea is less toxic than ammonia.

text: Which organ is the main organ of excretion in humans?
explanation: The kidneys are the primary excretory organs in humans. They filter blood, removing urea, excess salts, and water to produce urine. They also regulate blood pH and water balance.

text: The functional unit of the kidney is the
explanation: The nephron is the structural and functional unit of the kidney. Each kidney contains about one million nephrons. It consists of the Bowman's capsule, proximal tubule, loop of Henle, and distal tubule.

text: Glomerular filtration in the kidney filters blood based primarily on
explanation: Ultrafiltration occurs in the glomerulus under high hydrostatic pressure. Small molecules (water, glucose, urea, salts) pass into the Bowman's capsule, while large proteins and blood cells remain in the blood.

text: Which gland produces the hormone ADH (antidiuretic hormone)?
explanation: ADH (vasopressin) is produced by the hypothalamus and stored and released by the posterior pituitary gland. It acts on the collecting ducts of the kidney to increase water reabsorption.

text: The basic structural and functional unit of the nervous system is the
explanation: A neurone (neuron) is the basic unit of the nervous system. It is a specialised cell that transmits electrical impulses. Types include sensory, motor, and relay (interneuron) neurones.

text: A reflex arc consists of which sequence?
optionB: Receptor → Sensory neurone → Relay neurone → Motor neurone → Effector
explanation: A reflex arc is the neural pathway for a reflex action: receptor detects stimulus → sensory neurone → relay neurone (in spinal cord) → motor neurone → effector (muscle or gland) produces response.

text: The part of the brain responsible for balance and coordination of movement is the
explanation: The cerebellum coordinates voluntary movements, maintains posture and balance. It receives information from the sensory systems, spinal cord, and other parts of the brain to fine-tune motor activity.

text: Impulse transmission across a synapse is carried out by
explanation: Neurotransmitters (e.g., acetylcholine, dopamine) are chemical messengers released from the presynaptic terminal into the synaptic cleft. They diffuse across and bind to receptors on the postsynaptic membrane.

text: Which division of the nervous system controls involuntary functions like heartbeat and breathing?
explanation: The autonomic nervous system (ANS) regulates involuntary body functions. It has two divisions: sympathetic (fight or flight) and parasympathetic (rest and digest). It controls heart rate, digestion, and respiration rate.

text: Pollination is defined as the transfer of pollen grains from the
explanation: Pollination is the transfer of pollen grains from the anther (male part) to the stigma (female part) of a flower of the same or different species. It is a prerequisite for fertilisation in flowering plants.

text: Which of the following is an agent of wind pollination?
explanation: Wind-pollinated flowers have feathery or brush-like stigmas to catch pollen from the air. They also produce large amounts of light, smooth pollen and have small, dull flowers with no nectar.

text: The process by which a seed absorbs water and begins to grow is called
explanation: Germination is the process by which a seed sprouts and begins to grow into a new plant. It requires water, adequate temperature, and oxygen. The radicle (embryonic root) is usually the first structure to emerge.

text: Double fertilisation is a characteristic feature of
explanation: Double fertilisation is unique to angiosperms (flowering plants). One sperm fertilises the egg to form the zygote (2n), and the second sperm fuses with the two polar nuclei to form the endosperm (3n).

text: Vegetative reproduction by runners (stolons) is seen in
explanation: Strawberry plants reproduce vegetatively using runners (stolons), which are horizontal stems that grow along the ground and produce new plantlets at nodes. This is a form of asexual reproduction.

text: The testes in mammals produce
explanation: The testes (male gonads) produce testosterone, the primary male sex hormone. Testosterone is responsible for the development of male secondary sexual characteristics and sperm production.

text: In humans, fertilisation normally occurs in the
explanation: Fertilisation (the fusion of sperm and egg) normally occurs in the fallopian tube (oviduct), specifically in the ampulla region. The fertilised egg (zygote) then travels to the uterus for implantation.

text: The period of development of the foetus in the uterus is called
explanation: Gestation is the period from fertilisation to birth. In humans, the gestation period is approximately 9 months (38–40 weeks). During this time, the zygote develops into a fully formed foetus.

text: Which of the following is a secondary sexual characteristic in females?
explanation: Secondary sexual characteristics develop during puberty. In females, these include broadening of hips, development of breasts, pubic and underarm hair growth, and the onset of menstruation.

text: Primary growth in plants occurs at the
explanation: Primary growth occurs at apical meristems located at the tips of roots and shoots. It results in an increase in the length of the plant. This growth is due to cell division in meristematic tissue.

text: The S-shaped (sigmoid) growth curve in organisms represents
optionB: phases: lag, log (exponential), stationary, and decline
explanation: The sigmoid growth curve has four phases: (1) Lag phase - slow initial growth as organisms adapt; (2) Exponential/log phase - rapid growth; (3) Stationary phase - growth equals death; (4) Decline phase - population decreases.

text: Metamorphosis in insects that includes egg, larva, pupa, and adult stages is called
explanation: Complete metamorphosis (holometabolism) has four distinct stages: egg → larva → pupa → adult. Examples include butterflies, moths, beetles, and flies. Incomplete metamorphosis (hemimetabolism) has no pupal stage.

text: A gene is defined as
optionA: a segment of DNA that codes for a specific protein or trait
optionC: all the DNA in a cell
explanation: A gene is a specific sequence of DNA (deoxyribonucleic acid) that contains the information needed to produce a specific protein or functional RNA molecule. Genes are the units of heredity.

text: Gregor Mendel's Law of Segregation states that
optionB: two alleles for a trait separate during gamete formation
explanation: The Law of Segregation states that each organism has two alleles for each trait, and these alleles separate (segregate) during the formation of gametes so each gamete carries only one allele for each trait.

text: In a monohybrid cross between two heterozygous parents (Tt × Tt), what is the expected phenotypic ratio?
explanation: When Tt × Tt: genotypes produced are TT, Tt, Tt, tt in ratio 1:2:1. Since T (tall) is dominant over t (short), the phenotypic ratio is 3 tall : 1 short.

text: What term describes an organism with two identical alleles for a trait?
explanation: A homozygous organism has two identical alleles for a gene (e.g., TT or tt). A heterozygous organism has two different alleles (e.g., Tt). Homozygous dominant (TT) and homozygous recessive (tt) are both homozygous.

text: Colour blindness in humans is an example of
explanation: Colour blindness is caused by a recessive allele on the X chromosome. Males (XY) need only one copy of the allele to be colour blind, while females (XX) need two copies. Hence, it is more common in males.

text: The genotype of a carrier female for a sex-linked recessive trait is
explanation: A carrier female has one dominant (normal) allele and one recessive allele on her X chromosomes (X^C X^c). She has normal phenotype but can pass the recessive allele to her offspring.

text: Which of the following is the correct description of DNA structure?
optionB: Double helix of nucleotides with complementary base pairing
explanation: DNA (deoxyribonucleic acid) is a double helix consisting of two antiparallel strands of nucleotides. The bases pair specifically: adenine with thymine (A-T) and guanine with cytosine (G-C), held by hydrogen bonds.

text: The process by which DNA copies itself is called
explanation: DNA replication is the process by which a DNA molecule makes an exact copy of itself. It is semi-conservative — each new molecule consists of one original strand and one newly synthesised strand.

text: Charles Darwin's theory of evolution is based on
optionB: natural selection and survival of the fittest
explanation: Darwin proposed that evolution occurs through natural selection: individuals with favourable variations survive and reproduce more successfully. Over time, these beneficial traits become more common in the population.

text: Which of the following provides evidence for evolution?
explanation: Fossils are preserved remains of organisms from past geological periods. They provide direct evidence of the existence of ancient life forms and show how organisms have changed over time.

text: Analogous structures are organs that
optionA: have the same origin but different functions
optionB: have different origins but perform similar functions
explanation: Analogous structures (e.g., wings of birds and insects) perform similar functions but have different evolutionary origins. They are evidence of convergent evolution, not common ancestry.

text: Homologous structures are evidence for
explanation: Homologous structures (e.g., forelimbs of vertebrates) have the same basic structure and evolutionary origin but may perform different functions. They indicate common ancestry and divergent evolution.

text: Lamarck's theory of evolution proposed that
optionD: organisms do not change over time
explanation: Jean-Baptiste Lamarck proposed that characteristics acquired during an organism's lifetime (such as enlarged muscles) could be passed to offspring. This is now known to be incorrect, but it was an early evolutionary idea.

text: An ecosystem consists of
explanation: An ecosystem is a community of living organisms (biotic factors) interacting with each other and their non-living environment (abiotic factors such as soil, water, light, and temperature).

text: The position an organism occupies in a food chain is called its
explanation: A trophic level represents an organism's position in a food chain or food web based on the number of energy-transfer steps from the primary producer. Producers are at trophic level 1, primary consumers at level 2, etc.

text: Which of the following correctly represents a food chain?
explanation: A food chain shows the flow of energy from producer to consumers. Energy flows from: Grass (producer) → Rabbit (primary consumer) → Fox (secondary consumer). Arrows show direction of energy flow.

text: The total dry mass of living organisms in a given area is called
explanation: Biomass is the total mass of living organic matter (usually measured as dry mass to exclude water) in a given area or trophic level. It is used to construct ecological pyramids of biomass.

text: Decomposers in an ecosystem carry out which function?
optionB: Converting dead organic matter into inorganic nutrients
explanation: Decomposers (bacteria and fungi) break down dead organisms and organic waste into simpler inorganic compounds, returning nutrients to the soil. They are essential for nutrient cycling (e.g., the carbon and nitrogen cycles).

text: The carbon cycle involves which of the following processes?
explanation: The carbon cycle is the biogeochemical cycle by which carbon moves through the biosphere, atmosphere, and geosphere. Key processes include photosynthesis (removes CO₂), respiration, decomposition, and combustion.

text: Which type of ecological relationship benefits one organism while the other is harmed?
explanation: Parasitism is a relationship where one organism (parasite) benefits at the expense of another (host). The host is harmed but usually not immediately killed. Examples include tapeworm in the gut and Plasmodium in blood.

text: The nitrogen cycle involves bacteria that fix atmospheric nitrogen into
explanation: Nitrogen-fixing bacteria (e.g., Rhizobium in root nodules) convert atmospheric nitrogen (N₂) into ammonia (NH₃), which is then converted to nitrites and nitrates by nitrifying bacteria for plant use.

text: Overgrazing leads to which environmental problem?
explanation: Overgrazing removes plant cover, exposing topsoil to wind and water erosion. This leads to loss of soil fertility, degradation of land, and eventually desertification, particularly in semi-arid regions.

text: In which biome would you find the greatest biodiversity?
explanation: Tropical rainforests have the highest biodiversity of any biome, due to high rainfall, warm temperatures year-round, and high productivity. They cover about 6% of Earth's surface but contain over 50% of plant and animal species.

text: The passing of characteristics from parents to offspring is called
explanation: Heredity (inheritance) is the biological process by which traits are passed from parents to offspring through genes. Gregor Mendel's experiments with pea plants established the basic principles of heredity.

text: A mutation is best defined as
optionB: a permanent change in the DNA sequence of an organism
explanation: A mutation is a permanent, heritable change in the base sequence of DNA. Mutations can be spontaneous or induced by mutagens (e.g., UV radiation, certain chemicals) and may affect a single gene or an entire chromosome.

text: Down syndrome is caused by
explanation: Down syndrome (trisomy 21) occurs when a person has three copies of chromosome 21 instead of two. It results from non-disjunction during meiosis. It causes intellectual disability and characteristic physical features.

text: What is the role of meiosis in sexual reproduction?
optionA: Produces cells with double the chromosome number
optionB: Produces gametes with the haploid number of chromosomes
optionC: Produces identical cells to the parent
explanation: Meiosis is a type of cell division that produces gametes (sex cells) with half the normal chromosome number (haploid). When two gametes fuse during fertilisation, the normal diploid chromosome number is restored.

text: The process by which plants lose water as vapour through their leaves is called
explanation: Transpiration is the loss of water vapour from plant surfaces, mainly through stomata on leaves. It drives the upward movement of water (transpiration stream) and helps cool the plant.

text: Which of the following best describes the term 'osmoregulation'?
optionB: Regulation of water and solute balance in the body
explanation: Osmoregulation is the process by which organisms maintain the water and solute balance of their internal environment. In humans, the kidneys are the main osmoregulatory organs.

text: The liver detoxifies harmful substances and also produces
explanation: The liver produces bile, which is stored in the gall bladder and released into the duodenum to emulsify fats. The liver also detoxifies alcohol and drugs, breaks down amino acids, and stores glycogen.

text: Which of the following is a feature of insect-pollinated flowers?
optionC: Large, sticky pollen and nectar guides
explanation: Insect-pollinated flowers have adaptations to attract insects: large, colourful petals, scent, nectar, and sticky or spiny pollen that adheres to insects. The stigma is also sticky to trap pollen brought by insects.

text: Which of the following statements about growth is correct?
optionA: Growth involves only an increase in size
optionB: Growth is a permanent and irreversible increase in the size and dry mass of an organism
explanation: Growth is defined as a permanent, irreversible increase in the dry mass and size of an organism due to cell division (mitosis), cell enlargement, and cell differentiation. It requires energy from respiration.

text: Which of the following is an example of asexual reproduction in animals?
explanation: Budding is a form of asexual reproduction in Hydra (a freshwater organism) where a new individual grows as an outgrowth (bud) from the parent and eventually detaches to form a separate organism.

text: What is the function of the placenta in mammals?
optionB: Allows exchange of gases, nutrients and wastes between mother and foetus
explanation: The placenta is a temporary organ that connects the developing foetus to the mother's uterine wall. It allows for the exchange of oxygen, nutrients, and waste products between maternal and foetal blood without them mixing.

text: Which of the following disease is transmitted by the female Anopheles mosquito?
explanation: Malaria is caused by the Plasmodium parasite and transmitted through the bite of the female Anopheles mosquito. It is a leading cause of death in tropical regions including Nigeria.

text: The organism responsible for causing tuberculosis (TB) is
explanation: Tuberculosis is caused by the bacterium Mycobacterium tuberculosis. It primarily affects the lungs and is spread through airborne droplets when an infected person coughs or sneezes.

text: Which of the following is a deficiency disease?
explanation: Kwashiorkor is a severe form of protein-energy malnutrition caused by a diet very low in protein. It is common in young children and is characterised by oedema, a swollen belly, and growth retardation.

text: Immunisation works by
optionB: introducing antigens to stimulate antibody production
explanation: Immunisation (vaccination) introduces antigens (weakened or killed pathogens, or their proteins) into the body. The immune system responds by producing antibodies, creating immunological memory for future protection.

text: Which of the following is a basic life process common to all living organisms?
explanation: The basic life processes (MRS GREN) include: Movement, Respiration, Sensitivity, Growth, Reproduction, Excretion, and Nutrition. All living organisms must carry out these processes.

text: What does the acronym MRS GREN stand for in biology?
optionA: Minerals, Respiration, Sugar, Growth, Reproduction, Energy, Nutrition
optionB: Movement, Respiration, Sensitivity, Growth, Reproduction, Excretion, Nutrition
optionC: Motion, Rest, Sleep, Growth, Reproduction, Excretion, Nutrition
optionD: Movement, Reaction, Sensitivity, Growth, Respiration, Evolution, Nutrition
explanation: MRS GREN is a mnemonic for the seven characteristics of living organisms: Movement, Respiration, Sensitivity (irritability), Growth, Reproduction, Excretion, Nutrition. All living things exhibit these characteristics.

text: The spread of cholera is mainly through
explanation: Cholera is caused by the bacterium Vibrio cholerae and spreads through contaminated water and food. It causes severe watery diarrhoea and vomiting, leading to rapid dehydration. Good sanitation prevents its spread.

text: The process by which living organisms respond to changes in their environment is called
explanation: Irritability (sensitivity) is the ability of living organisms to detect and respond to stimuli (changes in the environment). Examples include plants growing toward light (phototropism) and animals reacting to pain.

text: Which of the following is a renewable source of energy?
explanation: Solar energy is a renewable energy source because it is continuously replenished by the sun. Fossil fuels (coal, petroleum, natural gas) are non-renewable because they take millions of years to form.

text: The removal of forests on a large scale is called
explanation: Deforestation is the large-scale clearing of forests for agriculture, logging, and urbanisation. It leads to habitat destruction, soil erosion, reduced biodiversity, and contributes to climate change.

text: Which of the following best describes a habitat?
optionA: The role of an organism in an ecosystem
optionB: The place where an organism lives
optionC: The total number of species in an area
explanation: A habitat is the natural environment where an organism lives and finds the food, water, shelter, and other conditions necessary for its survival. Examples include forests, rivers, deserts, and coral reefs.

text: What is the role of decomposers in a food web?
optionB: They recycle nutrients by breaking down dead matter
explanation: Decomposers (mainly bacteria and fungi) break down dead organic matter and waste products into simpler inorganic compounds. This releases nutrients back into the soil, making them available for plants to absorb.

text: In genetics, the physical appearance of an organism resulting from its genetic makeup is called its
explanation: Phenotype refers to the observable physical, biochemical, or behavioural characteristics of an organism, resulting from the interaction of its genotype and the environment. Examples: tall, blue eyes, round seeds.

text: The sex of a human offspring is determined by
explanation: Human females are XX and males are XY. The father contributes either an X or a Y sperm. If a Y sperm fertilises the egg (X), the offspring is male (XY); if an X sperm fertilises the egg (X), the offspring is female (XX).

text: Which of the following is NOT a function of the skeleton in vertebrates?
explanation: The skeleton provides support, protection for organs (e.g., skull protects the brain), facilitates movement (with muscles), produces blood cells (in bone marrow), and stores minerals. Photosynthesis is a plant function.

text: The process of converting glucose to glycogen for storage in the liver is called
explanation: Glycogenesis is the synthesis of glycogen from glucose, primarily in the liver and muscles. It is stimulated by insulin when blood glucose levels are high. This process stores excess glucose as glycogen.

text: Which of the following is an example of a saprophyte?
explanation: Saprophytes are organisms that feed on dead and decaying organic matter by secreting enzymes externally and absorbing the digested nutrients. Mushrooms (e.g., Agaricus) are classic saprophytic fungi.

text: Which vitamin is produced by the skin when exposed to sunlight?
explanation: Vitamin D is synthesised in the skin when exposed to ultraviolet (UV) radiation from sunlight. It is essential for calcium absorption and bone health. Deficiency causes rickets in children and osteomalacia in adults.

text: Kwashiorkor is a disease caused by deficiency of
explanation: Kwashiorkor results from severe protein deficiency. It commonly affects young children who have been weaned onto a low-protein diet. Symptoms include oedema, muscle wasting, and an enlarged abdomen.

text: Which of the following is a function of white blood cells?
explanation: White blood cells (leucocytes) are part of the immune system. Lymphocytes produce antibodies, and phagocytes (neutrophils and macrophages) engulf and destroy pathogens through a process called phagocytosis.

text: The law of independent assortment states that
optionA: alleles of a gene separate during gamete formation
optionB: genes on different chromosomes are inherited independently of one another
optionC: dominant alleles always mask recessive ones
explanation: Mendel's Law of Independent Assortment states that alleles of different genes assort independently of each other during gamete formation (assuming the genes are on different chromosomes/not linked).

text: Active transport differs from diffusion in that it
optionA: moves substances from high to low concentration
optionC: moves substances against the concentration gradient using energy (ATP)
explanation: Active transport moves substances against their concentration gradient (from low to high concentration). It requires cellular energy in the form of ATP and involves specific carrier proteins in the membrane.

text: The phylum Arthropoda includes animals with
explanation: Arthropods (e.g., insects, spiders, crabs) are characterised by a hard exoskeleton made of chitin, jointed appendages (legs, antennae), and a segmented body. They form the largest phylum in the animal kingdom.

text: In a pyramid of energy, which trophic level contains the most energy?
explanation: In an energy pyramid, producers (plants) at the base contain the most energy. Energy is lost as heat at each trophic level (approximately 90% is lost), so energy decreases as you move up the pyramid.

text: What is the main function of guard cells in leaves?
optionB: Regulating the opening and closing of stomata
explanation: Guard cells are specialised kidney-shaped cells that flank each stoma. They regulate the opening and closing of stomata by changes in their turgor pressure, controlling gas exchange and water loss in the plant.

text: Sickle cell anaemia is an example of
explanation: Sickle cell anaemia results from a point mutation in the gene encoding beta-globin. A single base change (GAG to GTG) causes glutamic acid to be replaced by valine, producing abnormal haemoglobin (HbS) and sickle-shaped red blood cells.

text: Which of the following is the correct description of the term 'ecology'?
optionC: The study of the relationships between organisms and their environment
explanation: Ecology is the branch of biology that studies the interactions between living organisms (biotic factors) and their physical environment (abiotic factors), including the flow of energy and cycling of nutrients.

text: The hardening of arteries due to fat deposits is called
explanation: Atherosclerosis is the build-up of fatty plaques (atheromas) on the inner walls of arteries, narrowing the lumen and reducing blood flow. It increases the risk of heart attack and stroke.

text: What type of nutrition do plants employ?
explanation: Plants use holophytic (autotrophic) nutrition. They manufacture their own food from inorganic raw materials (CO₂ and H₂O) using light energy in a process called photosynthesis.

text: Which of the following is an example of a gymnosperm?
explanation: Gymnosperms are seed-bearing plants whose seeds are not enclosed in a fruit (naked seeds). Examples include pine, fir, spruce, and cycads. Angiosperms have seeds enclosed within a fruit.

text: The organ in plants where gaseous exchange mainly takes place is
explanation: Gaseous exchange in plants mainly occurs in leaves through tiny pores called stomata. Oxygen and carbon dioxide diffuse in and out of the leaf. Some exchange also occurs through the roots (lenticels in stems too).

text: Excess amino acids in the body are broken down in the liver by a process called
explanation: Deamination is the removal of the amino group (–NH₂) from excess amino acids in the liver. The amino group forms ammonia (converted to urea), and the remaining carbon skeleton enters metabolic pathways for energy.

text: Which hormone regulates blood glucose levels by promoting the uptake of glucose by cells?
explanation: Insulin is produced by beta cells in the islets of Langerhans of the pancreas. It lowers blood glucose by stimulating body cells (especially liver and muscle) to take up glucose and convert it to glycogen (glycogenesis).

explanation: Pepsin is a protease enzyme secreted by chief cells in the stomach. It is activated by hydrochloric acid (HCl) and breaks peptide bonds in proteins, beginning protein digestion in the stomach.
